page: Amazon Web Services m7g.12xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture with the AWS Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. There are no integrated GPUs and no local storage is included, meaning storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory testing and strong performance in uncached memory bandwidth reads at 252.61 GB/sec and writes at 118.4 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores, alongside high throughput in software compilation and ray tracing. However, single-core performance is average, as shown in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core benchmarks. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the strong category, while large-model LLM inference speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton-based ARM architecture offers high resource density and memory bandwidth relative to its power profile. The primary tradeoff is the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated machine learning training. The instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
